questions.prompt: Describe the solution set of x + \(y=3\) in \(\mathbb R^2\) using parameter \(t=y\).
questions.answer: Let \(y=t\), where t is any real number. The equation x + \(y=3\) becomes x + \(t=3\), so \(x=3\) - t. Therefore the solution set is \((x, y)\) = \((3 - t, t)\), where t is any real number.

questions.prompt: Describe the solution set represented by RREF \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2&4\\0&1&-1&5\end{pmatrix}\) using \(z=t\).
questions.answer: The rows mean x + 2z = 4 and y - \(z=5\). Let \(z=t\). Then \(x=4\) - 2t and \(y=5\) + t. Therefore the solution set is \((x, y, z)\) = \((4 - 2t, 5 + t, t)\), where t is any real number.

questions.prompt: Classify the system represented by \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&1&-3\end{pmatrix}\) as having no solution, one solution, or infinitely many solutions.
questions.answer: The matrix has a pivot in every variable column and no contradictory row. It represents \(x=2\) and \(y=-3\). Therefore the system has exactly one solution.

questions.prompt: Classify the system represented by \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\) in variables x and y.
questions.answer: The second row represents 0x + 0y = 1, which is impossible. A contradictory row means the system is inconsistent. Therefore the system has no solution.

questions.prompt: Classify the system represented by \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}\) in variables x and y.
questions.answer: The row x + 2y = 0 gives one equation in two variables. There is no contradiction, and y is free. Let \(y=t\), so x = -2t. Therefore the system has infinitely many solutions: \((x, y)\) = \((-2t, t)\).

questions.prompt: Write the solution set of x - 2y + \(z=0\) in \(\mathbb R^3\) using \(y=s\) and \(z=t\).
questions.answer: Let \(y=s\) and \(z=t\), where s and t are real numbers. The equation x - 2y + \(z=0\) becomes x - 2s + \(t=0\). Solve for x: x = 2s - t. Therefore the solution set is \((x, y, z)\) = \((2s - t, s, t)\), with s and t real.

questions.prompt: Find the solution set of the homogeneous system represented by \(\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-3&0\\0&1&2&0\end{pmatrix}\), using \(z=t\).
questions.answer: The equations are x - 3z = 0 and y + 2z = 0. Let \(z=t\). Then x = 3t and y = -2t. Therefore the solution set is \((x, y, z)\) = \((3t, -2t, t)\) = t(3, -2, 1), where t is any real number.

questions.prompt: Explain why a homogeneous linear system always has at least one solution.
questions.answer: A homogeneous system has all right sides equal to zero. Setting every variable equal to zero makes every left side equal to zero because each left side is a linear combination of the variables. Therefore the zero vector always solves the system. This is called the trivial solution.

questions.prompt: For the solution set \((x, y, z)\) = \((1, 2, 0)\) + t(3, -1, 4), find the point corresponding to \(t=-2\).
A learner says a system with a free variable has no solution because one variable is unknown. Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: A free variable does not mean there is no solution. It means there are many possible values for that variable, and each choice gives a solution if the system is consistent. For example, x + \(y=3\) has y free if we let \(y=t\), and then \(x=3\) - t. This gives infinitely many solutions, not no solutions.
